summary.text: The Southern School … of Chinese painting, often called literati painting … is a term used to denote art and artists which stand in opposition to the formal Northern School
What the adherents of the Southern School valued was elegance, charm, good taste ; theirs (at least, as we know it from the Ming painter Shen Chou onwards) was essentially a happy art.

source.author: Arthur Waley
source.title: An Introduction to the Study of Chinese Painting
